## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the main change behaves as described. Without `--or-launch` a windowless app still exits 1 and nothing launches, so `omarchy hyprland focus app` and `omarchy-launch-browser` keep their focus-only contract. When a window exists, the helper focuses it and does not launch, even with `--or-launch --entry`. The lookup order (hint, `StartupWMClass`, entry id, `Name=`) resolves the PR's own fixtures as documented, Omarchy's own `omarchy-action` toasts never launch anything, and QML passes an argv array, so app names and hints do not reach a shell. The PR test passes 9/9 on the head, and it fails after 4 cases when run against the base helper, so the new cases exercise the new code.

Two issues are worth addressing, both small to fix.

### Click-launched apps inherit a pipe that closes when `gtk-launch` exits

The notification click runs the helper in the tracked `focusAppProc` `Process`, and the helper now ends in `exec setsid uwsm-app -- gtk-launch "$entry"`. In uwsm's default scope mode, `systemd-run --scope` execs in place, and GLib spawns the app with inherited stdout/stderr. So the launched app writes into Quickshell's pipes:

```text
focusAppProc (tracked Process, stdout/stderr = Quickshell pipes)
 └─ omarchy-hyprland-focus-app
     └─ exec setsid → uwsm-app → systemd-run --scope → gtk-launch
                                                        └─ app (inherits the same pipes)
gtk-launch exits → Qt cleanup() closes the read ends
app's next stdout/stderr write → EPIPE, or death by SIGPIPE if not ignored
```

A minimal offscreen Quickshell 0.3.1 run with stand-in scripts showed this: under a tracked `Process`, the stand-in app died with status 141 (SIGPIPE) on its first write after the tracked child exited. A control whose tracked child stayed alive wrote normally, and under `Quickshell.execDetached` stdout was `/dev/null` and the write succeeded.

**Impact:** apps that print to stdout/stderr and do not ignore SIGPIPE can be killed shortly after a toast click starts them. At minimum their output goes to a dead pipe. This matters most when the click starts a new long-lived process (restored or replayed toasts, multi-instance apps). A single-instance app that hands off to a running copy is mostly unaffected. No real application was observed dying, and D-Bus-activatable entries bypass this path. Every other launch path in the shell (`Util.execArgv`, `AppLibrary.launch`) is detached with null output.

**Suggested change:** redirect the launch branch's stdio in the helper, for example `exec setsid uwsm-app -- gtk-launch "$entry" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1`, or start the helper from QML with `Quickshell.execDetached(command)` as the other click paths do.

### The `--entry` hint is matched case-insensitively, with `XDG_DATA_HOME` first

`entry_hinted` uses `find ... -iname "$hint.desktop" -print -quit`, which returns the first case-insensitive match in data-dir order. Desktop file IDs are case-sensitive, and GIO resolves `gtk-launch`'s argument exactly. Omarchy installs its Discord web app as `~/.local/share/applications/Discord.desktop`, and `omarchy-webapp-install Slack` writes `Slack.desktop` there too:

| Args (synthetic entries) | Entry launched |
|---|---|
| `--or-launch --entry discord discord` (web app in `XDG_DATA_HOME`, native `discord.desktop` in `XDG_DATA_DIRS`) | `Discord.desktop` (web app) |
| `--or-launch --entry slack Slack` (web app `Slack.desktop` in `XDG_DATA_HOME`, native `slack.desktop` in `XDG_DATA_DIRS`) | `Slack.desktop` (web app) |
| `--or-launch Slack` (same entries, no hint) | `slack.desktop` (native, via `StartupWMClass`) |

**Impact:** a sender that names its own entry can get a different app launched, and the hint path undoes the native-over-web-app preference the PR describes for Slack. From a click, this applies to live notifications that carry a `desktop-entry` hint and have no `default` action. Restored or replayed toasts carry no hint and use the name steps. Whether Slack itself sends the hint was not established. The PR's table and test also treat `Discord.desktop` as native Discord, while on Omarchy that file name is the shipped web app.

**Suggested change:** look up the hint with exact case in each data dir first (for example `[[ -f $dir/$hint.desktop ]]`, then `$dir/$hint` when it already ends in `.desktop`), and fall back to `-iname` only when nothing matches exactly. A plain file test also stops `*`, `?` or `[` in a hint from acting as a glob. A test with the web app in `XDG_DATA_HOME` and the native entry in `XDG_DATA_DIRS` would cover this. The current fixtures share one directory, so data-dir precedence is not exercised.

**Minor notes:**
- `find` does not descend into a start point that is itself a symlink, so a symlinked `~/.local/share/applications` is skipped although `gtk-launch` would find its entries. `find -H` or a trailing `/` on each start point fixes this.
- The `Name=` step greps whole files, so it also matches `[Desktop Action]` names. For example, an app name `New Terminal` resolves to `foot.desktop`. Limiting the match to the `[Desktop Entry]` group avoids this.
- Entries in subdirectories of an `applications` dir (spec IDs such as `wine-Programs-App-App.desktop`) are never found because of `-maxdepth 1` plus `basename`. This gives the pre-PR "nothing happens" result, so it is not a regression. Resolving the hint through Quickshell's `DesktopEntries.byId` would cover these IDs and exact-case precedence together.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head `8af7c6a` against Quickshell, Qt, uwsm, GLib/GTK, Electron and freedesktop specification sources. The PR test and helper scenarios ran in an isolated sandbox with synthetic desktop entries and stubbed `hyprctl`, `uwsm-app` and `gtk-launch`. The pipe behavior was reproduced with Quickshell 0.3.1 offscreen and stand-in scripts, not real applications. No real desktop session, notification click or Slack/Discord client was tested, and the installed component versions on the tested Omarchy 4.0.4 system were not established.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted cross-checks of each other's findings, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
